monitored_text: Help Center Help Center CNC Machining Ordering CNC plastic material selection guide Help Center Ordering CNC Machining Ordering Sheet Metal Ordering CNC Machining Materials Aluminum CNC Machining Copper CNC Machining Plastic CNC Machining Stainless Steel CNC Machining Steel Alloy CNC Machining Sheet Metal Materials Aluminum Stainless Steel Alloy Steel CNC Machining Tutorials CNC Machining Design CNC Machining Knowledge Sheet Metal Tutorials Sheet Metal Design CNC Machine Basic Knowledge 5-Axis CNC Machine Privacy&Policies Coupon Policy Shipping Policies Policies CNC plastic material selection guide Last updated on Dec 17, 2024 CNC machining is a precise and efficient method for creating plastic parts for various industries. However, choosing the right plastic material is crucial to ensure that the final product meets your specifications and requirements. Here are some common plastic materials used for CNC machining, their advantages, disadvantages, suggested products, and specific data for their advantages: Epoxy Sheet - FR4 Advantages : High strength (tensile strength up to 340 MPa), excellent electrical insulation (in 90 ± 2 ℃ transformer oil: ≥ 40KV), resistance to flame (FV0), and moisture.Disadvantages: Limited temperature resistance (up to 130°C) and brittle. Suggested products : Circuit boards, electrical insulators, and aerospace components. Bakelite Advantages : High strength (compressive strength up to 260 MPa), durability, heat resistance (up to 160°C), and electrical insulation.Disadvantages: brittle and difficult to machine. Suggested products : Electrical switches, automotive parts, and appliance components. Cyclo-Steel-POM Advantages : High strength, stiffness, wear resistance (low friction coefficient), and dimensional stability.Disadvantages: it is difficult to be machined and may require specialized equipment. Suggested products : Gears, bearings, and precision mechanical components. ABS Engineering Plastic Advantages : Good impact resistance (notched impact strength up to 23 kJ/m2), toughness, and heat resistance (up to 80°C).Disadvantages: Low UV resistance and can warp under high temperatures. Suggested products : Automotive parts, toys, and consumer products. Nylon - PA6 Advantages : High strength (tensile strength up to 80 MPa), durability, wear resistance (low friction coefficient), and low friction.Disadvantages: Absorbs moisture (up to 9% water absorption) and can warp under high temperatures. Suggested products : Gears, bearings, and structural components. Acrylic Advantages : High transparency (light transmission up to 92%), optical clarity, and weather resistance.Disadvantages: Low impact resistance (notched impact strength around 0.5-1.5 kJ/m2) and can scratch easily. Suggested products : Displays, signage, and medical devices. Polycarbonate - PC Advantages : High impact resistance (notched impact strength up to 100 kJ/m2), heat resistance (up to 130°C), and optical clarity.Disadvantages: Low chemical resistance and can be prone to stress cracking. Suggested products : Safety goggles, automotive parts, and electronic components. Conclusion When a plastic material is selected for CNC machining, consider the mechanical properties, chemical resistance, thermal properties, cost, and machinability. It's essential to choose the right material for your specific application and requirements. Consult with a CNC machining service provider to help you make the right choice.
